title: How Agentic AI Will Reshape Payments (IMF Note 2026/004)
date_evidence: By Sonja Davidovic, Hervé Tourpe  April 24, 2026
key_claim: Agentic AI could shift payments from human-initiated instructions to agent-mediated decisions; the note uses a three-layer framework of intent, authorization and settlement and highlights the tension between probabilistic AI behaviour and the deterministic requirements of payment infrastructure, with KYC and multifactor authentication exposed because they rely on explicit human action.
notes: Primary multilateral anchor for the intent-authorization-settlement framing of the signal.

title: Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting on 27 March 2026
date_evidence: Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting on 27 March 2026  1 April 2026
key_claim: The FPC judged that financial firms had not yet adopted agentic AI in a manner presenting systemic risk, but that firms' private incentives to deploy agentic AI in payments and financial markets could fail to internalise negative externalities such as an increase in payments fraud; it asked the Bank and FCA to draw out risks from agentic AI deployment in payments and financial markets specifically.
notes: Tier 1 supervisory anchor; also supplies the counter-argument (no systemic risk yet, existing regulation flexible and outcomes-focused).

title: Regulatory Priorities: Payments (March 2026)
date_evidence: Regulatory Priorities  March 2026  Payments  Regulatory Priorities  Financial Conduct Authority
key_claim: In its first annual sector Regulatory Priorities report, the FCA states it will modernise payments regulation with the Treasury, including 'considering whether change or development of regulation is needed to support agentic AI payments' — the first time the regulator names agentic payments as a live policy question in a priorities document.
verbatim_quote: considering whether change or development of regulation is needed to support agentic AI payments
notes: Tier 1 regulator; first formal naming of agentic AI payments as a policy priority.

title: Agentic commerce and the battleground for new payments infrastructure
key_claim: Today's agent-payments landscape is fragmented across non-interoperable identity frameworks, payment protocols and communication layers; authentication is shifting from Know-Your-Customer to Know-Your-Agent, and a central question is what role a central authority should play in mandating agent identity and setting standards for agentic payments.
verbatim_quote: moving from Know-Your-Customer (KYC) to Know-Your-Agent (KYA) for payments
notes: Bank of England staff blog (DLT Lab); analytical staff view, classified Tier 2. Anchors the fragmentation and KYA framing.

title: Emerging trends for 2026, and other finance news to know (banking enters the agentic era)
key_claim: In 2026 the banking industry is moving from AI 'assistance' to 'transactional authority', with agentic systems integrated as semi-autonomous 'digital co-workers'; Lloyds Banking Group expects enterprise-wide agentic AI deployment to add about £100 million in value in 2026.
notes: Tier 2 institutional framing of the consensus narrative (the year of agentic AI in banking). Single structural anchor: 98 days before scan date, just outside the 90-day soft window, in the 3-6 month band.

title: Mastercard Unveils Open Standard to Verify AI Agent Transactions (Verifiable Intent)
key_claim: Mastercard, with Google, launched Verifiable Intent on 5 March 2026: an open-source framework linking a consumer's identity, instructions and transaction outcome into a tamper-resistant cryptographic audit trail for dispute resolution, designed to be agnostic to agentic protocols and built on FIDO Alliance, EMVCo, IETF and W3C standards, with commitments from Google, Fiserv, IBM, Checkout.com, Basis Theory and Getnet.
notes: Tier 3 quality fintech journalism; documents the network-set trust-layer standard and the dispute/liability rationale.

title: US card networks accelerate bets on agentic AI
key_claim: Visa and Mastercard are deploying agentic AI products into the network: Visa processed more than 106 million disputes globally in 2025 (up 35% since 2019) and launched AI dispute-resolution and a Trusted-Agent-Protocol bill-pay tie-up with Ramp (50,000+ corporate clients); Mastercard executed its first agentic payment in Hong Kong with HSBC, extending a network spanning the US, Australia and India.
notes: Tier 3 trade journalism; evidence the networks are racing to embed the agent-trust layer and the merchant/dispute economics at stake.
